question: Does the short-horizon momentum edge survive conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe?
action: Wrote and ran research/checks/momentum_cost_sensitivity.py: a predeclared cost grid (zero / realistic [repo realistic model: commission_per_trade=2.0, commission_per_share=0.003, slippage_cents=2.0, slippage_proportional=0.0005] / conservative [2x variable]) x lookback {3,5,10} x 10-asset universe, each cell run through the existing stress_segments regime gate with a matched coin-flip null (same cost cfg applied to the null), preceded by a signal-integrity gate. Wrote and ran research/checks/verify_momentum_cost_sensitivity.py, an independent path that re-implements the signal functions and recomputes via walk_forward + noise_benchmark (never calling stress_segments). Wrote and ran research/checks/diagnose_momentum_signal.py to confirm the defect. Ran the full regression suite and byte-compiled the new files.
verified: python3 research/checks/momentum_cost_sensitivity.py: ran end-to-end; manifest 10/10 OK; PREFLIGHT PASSED; leakage PASS (corrected momentum, AMZN/JPM); artifact written.

Signal-integrity gate: research.backtest.momentum_signals takes ONLY weight +1.0 at lookback 5 for 9/10 tickers (AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/META/TSLA/JPM/JNJ/XOM frac_long=1.000); NVDA takes both signs only because its early adjusted close is below 1.0 (min log price -1.803). Contracted turnover ~0.0002-0.0007 vs a genuine momentum signal ~0.24-0.55. DEGENERATE=True.

Contracted signal positive-edge assets across zero/realistic/conservative cost = 6 / 6 / 6 at lookback 5, with per-asset medians identical across all three cost levels (e.g. AAPL [0.071,0.054,0.092,0.069]); i.e. costs never bite because turnover ~0.

Corrected (genuine) momentum, sign of the lookback log return, positive-edge assets = 0 / 0 / 0 at lookback 5 -> classification NO_ZERO_COST_EDGE; at zero cost the counts are REGIME_STABLE=3 (each with a negative segment, so not a positive edge), CONSISTENT_WITH_NOISE=6, REGIME_DEPENDENT=1.

python3 research/checks/verify_momentum_cost_sensitivity.py: Gate 1 signal-integrity reimplementation reproduces the degeneracy (MATCH on AAPL/AMZN/NVDA/JPM x lookbacks); Gate 2 fresh walk_forward+noise_benchmark recomputation MATCHES the artifact on all AMZN/JPM x lookback{3,5,10} x cost{zero,realistic,conservative} x variant{contracted,corrected} candidate AND null medians; Gate 3 determinism identical.

python3 -m py_compile on the three new files: OK (no output).

Diagnosis of the mechanism: momentum_signals line 911 computes np.mean(np.log(closes[i-lookback+1:i+1])) -- the sign of an average PRICE LEVEL, not a return -- so it is lookback-independent; this explains the identical candidate medians across lookbacks 3/5/10 recorded in momentum_results.json and momentum_lookback_sweep_results.json.
unverified: The independent verifier recomputed only the AMZN and JPM cells via a second path; the remaining 8 tickers' corrected/contracted cells rely on the check's internal determinism plus the structural signal-integrity proof, not a second independent recomputation.

The corrected momentum signal was evaluated on the cost grid but its per-asset medians were only inspected for lookback 5 in this report; lookbacks 3/10 corrected cells are in the artifact but not narrated here.

The framework function research.backtest.momentum_signals was NOT modified (out of scope for R-001); the entire prior momentum evidence chain (momentum.py, momentum_lookback_sweep.py, momentum_longer_horizon.py, cross_sectional_momentum, breakout_20day_cont) remains based on the degenerate signal and is now suspect pending a corrected re-run.

Whether a corrected momentum signal has a genuine edge at any lookback/holding period is not established here; the zero-cost NO_ZERO_COST_EDGE result is specific to the sign-of-lookback-log-return, 1-day-hold implementation tested.
observed_effect: R-001's cost-sensitivity check surfaced a decisive defect that inverts the interpretation of the prior positive evidence. research.backtest.momentum_signals computes sign(mean(log(close))) over the lookback window -- an average price level, always positive for these assets -- so the signal is (near) always-long and effectively lookback-independent (9/10 tickers always-long at lookback 5; turnover ~0.0002 vs ~0.4 for a genuine momentum signal). Therefore the prior 'momentum edge' (7/10 REGIME_STABLE, positive; admitted as candidate positive evidence) is a near-constant long equity position, not a momentum anomaly, and its apparent cost robustness is spurious: positive-edge assets are 6 -> 6 -> 6 across zero/realistic/conservative cost because near-zero turnover means costs never bite (per-asset medians are byte-identical across cost levels). A correctly-specified momentum signal (sign of the previous lookback-day log return, defined a-priori from the class docstring) shows 0 uniformly-positive REGIME_STABLE assets even at ZERO cost (3 REGIME_STABLE but each with a negative segment), so there is no genuine short-horizon momentum edge whose cost robustness could be positive. Net: the cost-robustness question resolves negatively and the candidate positive momentum evidence is invalidated.
uncertainty_targeted: Whether the short-horizon momentum edge survives conservative transaction-cost stress on the collected real-data universe.
uncertainty_reduced: Decisively reduced. The 'momentum edge' is an artifact of a degenerate always-long signal, not a momentum anomaly; a correctly-specified short-horizon momentum signal has no zero-cost edge, so momentum cost robustness is moot; the prior candidate positive momentum evidence is invalidated. Also established that a genuine momentum signal would carry ~0.4 turnover (material cost sensitivity), so any future momentum test must be re-run after fixing the signal, and that reuse-based verifiers (importing momentum_signals) cannot catch such a defect.
research_result: No genuine short-horizon momentum edge exists on the collected universe. The contracted momentum_signals is degenerate (always-long, ~0 turnover), so the prior 7/10 REGIME_STABLE positive edge is a constant long equity position and its cost robustness is spurious (6->6->6 across zero/realistic/conservative). A correctly-specified momentum signal (sign of the lookback log return) shows no uniformly-positive REGIME_STABLE edge at zero cost (NO_ZERO_COST_EDGE). The candidate positive momentum evidence should be REJECTED pending a corrected-signal re-run; the momentum cost-robustness classification is not 'robust' but 'no genuine edge to be robust'.
